text:
Maya Chen: incident-bot paging on prod Dedicated pools in us-east. Alerts show sustained queue depth and tokens/sec throttling for multiple customers. Seeing 5xx spikes starting ~10:30 UTC.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Dedicated pool `dedicated-prod-east` sustained queue > 95% for 7m. Escalation: eng-oncall. Incident ID: INC-20260315-31.

Maya Chen: I'm on it, taking initial triage. Quick ask: did autoscaler fail to add nodes? Dashboard shows target size stuck at 8 but queue implies we should be at 20.

Simon Reyes: I can pull logs. Looks like the autoscaling controller had repeated 429 from cloud provider around 10:25 -> 10:33, then backoff. Those rate limits prevented scale-up.

Aj Patel: Copy. Paging now to infra on-call (Nora). @Nora Li can you confirm if provider-side quotas are the issue or if our controller is misconfigured?

Nora Li: looking. Provider reports "API rate limit exceeded" for autoscale requests. It's a burst of small customers hitting us and our controller is being throttled. We have option to: 1) toggle Dedicated burst capacity (reserve capacity fallback), 2) apply rapid client-facing rate limiting, 3) temporarily increase committed capacity if feasible.

Maya Chen: Prioritize customer impact mitigation first. Which customers are affected? Console traces show elevated latencies for orgs: "FastMailCo", "EduPilot", and several small PLG signups. Not seeing data exfil; just degraded latencies and some 503s.

Aj Patel: I'm going to push an emergency route-level rate limit for non-enterprise orgs to reduce token ingestion by ~60%. Command via admin API: 
```
POST /admin/routing/limits
{
  "selector": "tier:plg",
  "requests_per_minute": 100,
  "reason": "emergency surge -- reduce load while autoscaler recovers"
}
```

Simon Reyes: applied the rate-limiter rule, console shows incoming qps drop ~55% within 2 mins. Good short-term win.

Nora Li: Meanwhile I'm enabling reserved burst capacity on the dedicated pool as an emergency toggle. This doesn't depend on provider scaling API. Running: 
```
rb-admin toggle-burst --pool dedicated-prod-east --enable --duration 10m
```

infra-bot: Action recorded: rb-admin toggled burst (user: Nora Li) pool=dedicated-prod-east duration=10m trace=trace-7a9

Maya Chen: Nice. Enabling burst removed immediate queue pressure, tokens/sec normalized. However burst has limits and we need autoscaler to restore long term capacity.

Aj Patel: I'm working on the autoscaler controller logs now. Found that the controller's refresh token to provider expired and our refresh retry path had a bug: it retried with exponential backoff but didn't refresh creds after 5xx. Fix is small: call refresh_token() before retry after 3 consecutive 429/5xx. Pushing a canary hotfix to the controller deployment.

Simon Reyes: Suggested patch: 
```
# prod autoscaler patch
if response.status in [429, 500, 502, 503]:
  if consecutive_errors >= 3:
    refresh_provider_creds()
  backoff()
```

Nora Li: Can we also extend the burst duration to cover deployment? I can bump to 30m if we think fixes will take longer.

Maya Chen: Yes, extend to 30m. Also note we should notify customers in affected org list and offer credit. Aj, can you draft a short customer incident note for support? Keep it factual.

Aj Patel: Drafting now: 
"We experienced elevated errors and latency between 10:25–11:15 UTC due to autoscaling controller failing to request additional nodes. We applied emergency burst capacity and rate limits to stabilize traffic; a patch is deployed and autoscaling is recovering. We're offering a credit; support will follow up with impacted accounts"

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-31 severity=P1 assigned_to=Maya Chen.

Maya Chen: Handoff note: I'll remain as lead for the next 20 minutes then hand to Aj for postmortem & customer comms. @Aj Patel you ok to take the 11:00–12:00 handoff?

Aj Patel: Taking handoff at 11:00 UTC. I'll run the postmortem checklist and coordinate with support.

Simon Reyes: Canary hotfix merged and deployed to autoscaler at 10:56 UTC. Watching metrics. Logs show provider token refresh succeeding now.

Maya Chen: Autoscaler now incremented the pool from 8 -> 18 by 11:04 UTC (confirmed). Queue depth dropped to normal baseline and 5xx stabilized.

Nora Li: Burst toggle auto-expiry scheduled at 11:26 UTC (30m). Once autoscaler is stable we should disable burst to avoid unexpected billing. I'll set an automated task to disable unless overridden.

Aj Patel: Removing the emergency PLG rate limits at 11:12 UTC. Verified no spike after removal.

Maya Chen: Summary for the incident channel: cause = provider API rate limits + autoscaler credential refresh bug; mitigation = emergency rate-limiting for low-tier customers, enabled reserved burst capacity, deployed autoscaler hotfix; impact = transient 5xx/latency for several orgs from 10:25–11:04 UTC; resolution = autoscaler recovered and burst removed/scheduled.

Maya Chen: Action items: 
- Simon: submit PR with unit/regression test for refresh logic (due EOD).
- Nora: add provider quota monitoring + alert (due tomorrow).
- Aj: coordinate customer communications and credits (start now).
- Maya: write incident timeline and runbook updates for burst toggle and when to apply rate limits (due tomorrow).

Aj Patel: Noted. I'll open support tickets for FastMailCo and EduPilot and attach logs.

Maya Chen: Closing page for ops. If anything regresses ping here and we'll reopen. Thanks team :thumbsup:
